items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: I went in behind Cab Calloway, Lunceford's band did, while Sammy Greer -- you know him -- he was playing drums for Duke Ellington... all the drummers that appeared in the Cotton Club with those bands had fabulous drum outfits

ctx.x: Cab Calloway, Duke Ellington and the big bands like that -- well, Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington I knew. On top of that, Stanley, I went in behind Cab Calloway, Lunceford's band did, while Sammy Greer -- you know him -- he was playing drums for Duke Ellington, and all the drummers that appeared

in the Cotton Club with those bands had fabulous drum outfits, gongs, chimes, vibraphones, timpanies, all kind of drums hanging around. It was a beautiful setting for those bands. Well, Stocks told Harold Oxley and Jimmie Lunsford, now, your drummer got to have some drums up there. I was sitting up there with a bass drum and one cymbal. He said, no, we used to seeing drums in here, make a beautiful setting for the band.
